task.title: Drag and drop vertically within a column doesn't scroll
task.description:
For a column with a lot of tasks, a user may want to drag a task to reorder it beyond the current viewport of the column. However trying to drag a task above or below the viewport doesn't scroll the column, so it isn't possible to reorder a task more than a few spaces at a time.

Fix: dragging a task above or below the fold of a column smoothly scrolls the column in that direction.

## Shipped (2026-08-15, PR #105)

One PR through a two-round adversarial execution-verified review (record on the PR), all evidence from real Chrome over CDP.

A requestAnimationFrame loop scrolls the hovered column's own scroller while a drag's remembered cursor sits in a min(72px, 25%) edge zone — speed linear to 900px/s, frame delta capped at 50ms (an 892ms main-thread stall steps 44px, no teleport), with a sub-pixel remainder carry because Chrome rounds scrollTop (without it the slow end of the ramp stalls). The drop marker recomputes every frame the column moves, so placement stays exact under a stationary cursor across full-column scrolls. Baseline measured: Chrome's native drag autoscroll dies ~20px from the edge, which is why the bug read "doesn't scroll".

The review caught two things worth remembering. First, a drop could be SILENTLY LOST after autoscrolling: Blink fires dragover only while the hit-test target is unchanged, and the scroll churns that target under a stationary cursor, so Chrome re-asks droppability via dragenter — which the page never cancelled — and skips the drop (full scroll, zero writes, no error; probabilistic on what sits under the cursor at release). Fixed by accepting dragenter through the same single dragDestination() as dragover, with the parity table pinning the two targets where droppable and drop-target differ. Second, the story's literal gesture — the cursor shoved PAST the column — still didn't scroll while a fake-DOM-only test claimed it did; vertical overshoot now keeps the last column scrolling (both overshoot sites independently load-bearing on disjoint event paths), sideways exits still stop, and the end-to-end gesture (past the bottom, 1644px of scroll, return, drop) lands with one write. Also corrected: a false "Chrome reports no relatedTarget" justification (measured false; the coordinate leave rule stands as Firefox/Safari robustness, with fixtures driving both browser shapes honestly).

Zero leaked rAF callbacks on every termination path (drop, cancel, out-of-window release, mid-drag navigation, back-to-back gestures); mid-drag polls unbroken; 60fps parked, 59fps at full scroll. Residuals: the horizontal equivalent (dragging toward an off-screen column) confirmed real and left for a follow-up story; the status-reorder panel shares the accept-flag defect class dormantly, filed as WB-01M03KYNR7SCV5ZEA7H68C0922. The one CI failure before merge was a runner-side git object-database permission flake in an untouched test; green on re-run.
